source_loc.method: Framework counts are physical lines in the two new runtime contract modules, their two focused tests, deployment YAML/HCL/new workflows, and focused new docs. Custom counts are the complete pinned Layer 15 repository reported by a read-only audit; scopes are not equivalent and must not be treated as a code-efficiency ratio.

runtime_dependencies.candid_note: Framework delegates workflow queue/history/timer/signal/retry mechanics to managed Temporal and adds a managed control-plane dependency. Custom keeps Redis transport non-authoritative but owns queue leases, heartbeat, redelivery, and workflow recovery code.

configuration_and_topology.assessment: Framework has more queue-specific Deployments and disruption/scaling objects because Temporal/LangGraph/evidence/remediation/memory/sandbox/protocol workers are isolated. Custom has an explicit data and egress namespace plus Redis and a separate UI image.

self-hosted Temporal frontend/history/matching/worker services and their persistence/visibility databases
Temporal server schema upgrade, shard sizing, replication and control-plane patch automation
custom graph scheduler, synchronized fan-in, reducer and checkpoint mechanics
hand-written infrastructure module dependency code by using direct exact-pinned Terraform resources

application ledger, dual hashes, idempotency, inbox/outbox and projections
budget reservation, provider/connector quotas, retry ownership and backpressure
approval, fencing, receipts, verification, reconciliation and compensation
evidence/memory provenance, citations, retention, legal hold and archive policy
sandbox policy, artifact trust, cleanup and isolation readiness
MCP/A2A trust, workload identity, content bounds and proposal-only effects
migration compatibility, restore acceptance, generation fencing and routing
release approval, admission exceptions, SLO/error-budget policy and compliance evidence

temporal_tradeoff.framework: Temporal Cloud through PrivateLink; namespace/task-queue isolation, payload codec, API key/mTLS, Worker Deployment/build IDs, replay, rate/concurrency, retention, schedule-to-start, drain and reconciliation remain explicit.
temporal_tradeoff.custom: No workflow framework. PostgreSQL ledger plus Redis Streams and custom workers/reconciler own transport, leases, heartbeat, redelivery and durable workflow semantics.
temporal_tradeoff.assessment: Managed Temporal removes substantial server and queue mechanics but adds usage cost, vendor/region/DPA/retention qualification, history/versioning APIs, payload privacy, namespace operations and managed failover assumptions. Neither option replaces application truth or effect controls.

supply_chain_comparison.framework_difference: Framework reuses the custom Layer 15 GitHub/Sigstore pattern with existing uv/npm locks and one combined application/BFF/UI image. Protected-branch enforcement and commit signing remain external and unproven.

cost_and_capacity.framework_reference: Three system and three Kata nodes minimum, three NAT gateways, Multi-AZ db.r7g.xlarge RDS, interface endpoints, S3/KMS/Backup/logs/AMP, plus Temporal Cloud usage.
cost_and_capacity.custom_reference: Three m7g.large system nodes, sandbox scale-to-zero, db.t4g.medium RDS, two cache.t4g.small Redis nodes, NAT/log/backup/telemetry.
cost_and_capacity.assessment: Framework defaults favor stronger sandbox and database headroom but likely cost more at idle. Neither repository contains prices, storage-growth measurements, provider quotas, load curves, budget alerts, or a validated capacity model.
